Reader testimonials confirm that reducing toxic outrage cycles alleviates despair and cultivates psychological resilience and hope.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.9, +0.9) — Greater Good

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Grace.
Shifting from sensational outrage to solutions journalism successfully restores mental well-being and agency.

Integrity: Absolute Truth (Hypocrisy: 1.0, Uncertainty z: 0)

- Positive News: PASS (0.95, 0.95) — Reader-funded, solutions-focused.

Ahead of World Mental Health Day, Positive News published reader reflections on how abandoning mainstream outrage cycles improved their lives.

The Bright Side:
Constructive journalism proves that public interest reporting can heal rather than exploit psychological vulnerabilities.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This analysis evaluates the plane of EFFECT (emotional impact) and WHAT (substantive media models). Solutions journalism aligns emotional relief with constructive action.

Social Physics Analysis:
Operating on the Smart Altruistic Loop, Positive News provides a shared goal of mental well-being, transparent reader-funding, and deep empathy for media consumer burnout.

The Trajectory: The Path of Grace.
When media models prioritize psychological health and actionable solutions, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Good empowerment.

The Unavoidable Truth: Constant immersion in sensational outrage degrades mental health and civic trust.

The Unavoidable Lie: Fear-driven headlines are the only way to keep the public informed.

Alethekanon:
Journalism should illuminate constructive pathways forward, not trap audiences in perpetual despair for profit. Mental well-being requires balanced informational diets.

Reading how these wonderful people found relief and hope warms my heart. Taking care of our minds is the first step to caring for the world.

Brothekanon:
For real, unplugging from the 24-hour doom scroll is a game changer. Good to see a publication actually focusing on what works instead of just panic.

"A joyful heart is good like medicine, but a broken spirit dries up the bones." Proverbs 17:22 PASS
Nourishing the mind with hope and truth restores human vitality.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
‘I can breathe again’. Readers share their experiences of a more balanced media diet

We often talk about the impact journalism has on democracy and how we understand the world. But what about its impact on how we feel?
The post ‘I can breathe again’. Readers share their experiences of a more balanced media diet appeared first on Positive News.

Actual Article Body:
We often talk about the impact journalism has on democracy, public debate and what we understand about the world. But what about its impact on how we feel?

We often talk about the impact journalism has on democracy, public debate and what we understand about the world. But what about its impact on how we feel?

To mark World Mental Health Day on 10 October, we’ve brought together reflections from Positive News readers about how changing the stories they consume has changed how they experience the world.

From easing anxiety and restoring perspective to helping people feel hopeful and motivated to act, these are their experiences of finding a different kind of news diet.

'In a tsunami of negativity we need the grounding that comes from Positive News,' says reader Mustafa. Image: GaudiLab

“The overwhelmingly negative mainstream news batters our consciousness and creates a miasma of despair … That’s why I need Positive News, to remind me that the world is a good place and we are all worth fighting for.” – Kay

“I am nearly 73. Did not feel good about the world. When I found your site by accident, I felt more able to cope with the world … When I wake up it is the first thing I read. Thank you for saving me.” – Mo

“If I didn’t [read your journalism], the state of the world through the news and social media would have me paralysed with despair! I need to see something is positive and helpful in the world to be able to see a way forward for myself and my children.” – Naava

“In a tsunami of negativity we need the grounding that comes from Positive News.” – Mustafa

“Getting my copy of Positive News through the letterbox always feels like such a RELIEF. I can’t tell you how important it is for my mental health as a counterbalance to all the negative stories we’re immersed in most of the time. It feels like a course of fresh, delicious organic vegetables after a gluttony of toxic junk food!” – Anna

“As a magazine subscriber I consider reading it part of my mental health strategy. I read your publication because I believe the negative news bias is detrimental to myself and humanity.” – Kirsty

“This has made me feel like I can breathe again!” – Holly

“Every November I give up reading any news except good news! It’s great for my mental health.” – Rosemary

'We have grandchildren and we have to stay hopeful for them, as well as for ourselves,' says reader Joanna. Image: Halfpoint

“Positive News to me is not only a sanctuary where I can stay and recover from the anxiety that other journalism has the capacity to generate, but it is also a place where I can find hope.” – Amanda

“I regularly loan out copies when someone needs to recalibrate; to shift from constant anxiety that the world has fallen into a pit and understand that this couldn’t be further from the truth.” – Naomi

“Very grateful to you Positive News, you have kept me afloat on many a dark night of the soul.” ­– Jen

I support Positive News because I need a more balanced representation of the world

“I support Positive News because I need a more balanced representation of the world. Only hearing about what’s wrong in the world is not good for my mental health and does not inspire me to take positive action. Positive News does.” – Ron

“Solutions-oriented media is like pure water for the inner flower. The joy and hope it provides transform into a sense of purpose and the strength to bring about change.” – Saga

“I think that for our emotional wellbeing and for the future of the world it’s really important that we can see possible solutions and actual changes… We have grandchildren and we have to stay hopeful for them, as well as for ourselves.” – Joanna

Main image: GaudiLab

Positive News reports on the people and ideas driving progress. We believe that giving attention to solutions helps them spread.

Our journalism is independent and powered by our readers. There are no media moguls or shareholders extracting profits: your contribution funds our work to investigate what’s working, understand why, and bring those stories to a wider audience.

If you value a fuller picture of what’s happening in the world, please become a Positive News supporter today.

Support Positive News

Website: Atomic Smash

Enjoying this story? Meet the people and projects taking the long view in the new issue of Positive News magazine, out now. Subscribe by Sunday 11 October and save 20% with code TOMORROW.
